banner: OpenAI 内部推理速度开始外卖
banner_en: OpenAI's in-house inference speed goes on sale

image.caption: 本期头版配图：Cerebras CS-4 晶圆级推理平台。OpenAI 靠它把自家模型跑到比 GPU 快 14 倍，这套系统现在开始向企业客户开放。（图：Latent Space 播客对话 Cerebras CTO Sean Lie 的视频截图）
image.caption_en: This issue's lead image: Cerebras' CS-4 wafer-scale inference platform. OpenAI uses it to run its own models 14x faster than on GPUs, and the system is now opening up to enterprise customers. (Image: from Latent Space Podcast's interview with Cerebras CTO Sean Lie)

actions.text: 今晚花十分钟，从你手头正在用或正在搭的 agent 工具或 skill 里，挑一个负责“查东西”的工具（搜代码、查文档、找记录都算），看它返回结果时是只给一个位置或 ID，还是直接把有用的内容摆在结果里。今天这篇实测数据说得很直白：同一个语义检索后端，只把“返回文件名加行号”改成“直接带上那行代码”，agent 不用再多翻一次文件确认，重命名任务的一次通过率从 0.67 涨到 0.83，多余的确认读取从平均 15.2 次砍到 3.2 次。完成标志：写下你挑的这个工具现在是哪一种返回形状，以及要不要现在就把它改成“直接给答案”这种形状。
actions.text_en: Spend ten minutes tonight picking one "lookup" tool in an agent/skill you're using or building (code search, doc search, log search, anything that fetches info), and check whether it returns just a location/ID or puts the useful content directly in the result. Today's study makes the case with hard numbers: changing the exact same semantic-search backend from "return a file path and line number" to "return that line's actual code" raised rename-task pass@1 from 0.67 to 0.83 and cut follow-up confirmation reads from an average of 15.2 down to 3.2, with nothing else changed. Done when you've named which shape your chosen tool currently returns, and whether you're changing it to "just give the answer" tonight.

actions.text: 如果你自己维护一个想被开发者或 coding agent 选中的产品或服务（哪怕只是内部工具的说明页），花十分钟按今天这篇研究的思路自查一遍你的落地页或 README：有没有把免费额度、保留期限、多合一打包这些细节写得含糊，或者堆了一堆 agent 用不上的功能在同一个定价里。今天的数据显示，Supabase 常常不是输在能力上，是输在页面上把认证、存储这些附加功能打包进数据库定价，被 agent 判定为“超出需求”；Mailgun 则常常因为免费额度页面一行“1 天保留”直接出局。完成标志：写下你检查的这个产品或页面有没有类似的表述问题，以及打算怎么改。
actions.text_en: If you maintain any product or service (even an internal tool's docs page) that you'd want a developer or coding agent to pick, spend ten minutes auditing your landing page or README using today's study as a checklist: is any free-tier limit, retention period, or bundled feature written vaguely, or does your pricing bundle in capabilities an agent isn't even asking for? Today's data shows Supabase often loses not on capability but on presentation: agents read auth/storage/realtime bundled into its database pricing and judge it as "more than the ask." Mailgun regularly loses on one line reading "1-day retention" on its free tier. Done when you've written down whether your product/page has a similar wording problem and what you'd change.

actions.text: 今天这篇账算下来，一个能独立管几十个子 agent 的“初级 AI 工程师”，现在跑一小时大概 6 美元。花十分钟翻一下你自己因为“工作量太大、没空做”被搁置的一个小项目或工具（个人网站重做、账目整理、旧内容重新整理这类，作者今天正好都提了一遍），估一下如果现在用一个能自主管理子 agent 批次的模型去跑，值不值得重新捡起来。完成标志：写下这个项目的名字，以及你觉得现在值不值得启动。
actions.text_en: Today's math works out to about $6 an hour for a "junior AI engineer" that can independently manage dozens of subagents. Spend ten minutes going through one small project or tool you shelved because it seemed like too much work (a personal site rebuild, finance cleanup, reorganizing old content, the author happened to list exactly these today), and estimate whether it's worth picking back up now that a model can manage the subagent fleet itself. Done when you've named the project and your one-line verdict on whether it's worth starting now.

hands_on.title: 去 Cerebras 免费 playground，亲自感受一下 1000+ tokens/秒
hands_on.title_en: Try Cerebras' free playground and feel 1,000+ tokens/sec yourself
hands_on.why: 今晚头条说的是 Cerebras 的推理速度快到能把原本要等的 agent 循环变成实时对话，这种“快”光看数字很难有实感。Cerebras Cloud 有免费开发者层，能直接在网页 playground 里对着开源模型打字，回复几乎是瞬间刷出来的，比读任何一篇评测都更直接地感受到“批处理变成实时”具体是什么意思。
hands_on.why_en: Tonight's banner story is about inference so fast that an agent loop that used to mean waiting becomes real-time, and a number alone doesn't really convey that. Cerebras Cloud has a free developer tier with a web playground you can type into directly against an open-weight model, with replies streaming back almost instantly, a much more direct feel for what "batch becomes real-time" actually means than reading any benchmark writeup.
steps: 打开 https://cloud.cerebras.ai/，用邮箱免费注册一个开发者账号
进入网页版 Chat Playground，不需要写代码
选一个可用的开源模型（如 Llama 或 Qwen 系列），输入一个稍长的问题，比如让它写一段几百字的说明或做一次多步推理
盯着回复刷新的速度，感受一下这是不是比你平时用的 AI 产品明显更快
steps_en: Open https://cloud.cerebras.ai/ and sign up free with an email
Go to the web Chat Playground, no code required
Pick an available open-weight model (Llama or Qwen family) and ask it something with some length, a few-hundred-word explanation or a multi-step reasoning question
Watch how fast the reply streams back and compare it to whatever AI product you normally use

meta_read:
今晚几条线放在一起看，说的其实是同一件事：AI 这场竞争，决胜点已经从“模型好不好”挪到了“谁的东西能被 agent 这套调用循环直接吃下去”。grep 赢 LSP，不是因为它更聪明，是因为它一次返回的信息形状，agent 不用再多问一句就能用；Stripe 赢 PayPal、Neon 赢 Supabase，也不是产品能力上的差距，是 agent 读到的页面信息和定价打包方式，直接决定了谁被选中、谁只是被提一句就路过；Two Sigma 解决“agent 能不能放心用”这道题，靠的也不是等模型自己变得更可信，是把身份和网络访问这两处架构先钉死。三条线合起来，能力这一层的军备竞赛还在继续（Cerebras、Arm 都在抢 agent 处理器这门生意），但真正决定谁能把这份能力变现的，越来越是接口、页面、身份这些看起来不起眼的工程细节，不是模型跑分。

第二条值得单独记一句：Astra 的“6 美元一小时”和 Cerebras“提速 14 倍”这两笔账放一起看，说明干一件事的成本正在快速逼近可以忽略的水平。但同一天 Two Sigma 和 Armature 这两篇分享都在说，便宜之后真正卡人的不是钱，是信任和分发：谁的 agent 敢真的自主花这几块钱，谁的产品能被 agent 自主选中，这两道题目前都还没有现成答案。
meta_read_en:
Tonight's threads point at the same shift: the real competition in AI has moved from "is the model good" to "can this thing be consumed directly by an agent's own decision loop." Grep beats LSP not because it's smarter, but because the shape of what it returns needs no follow-up question. Stripe beats PayPal, and Neon beats Supabase, not on product merit, but because of how a page reads and how a price is bundled, deciding who actually gets picked versus who just gets mentioned in passing. Two Sigma solves "can we trust an agent with real access" the same way, not by waiting for models to become trustworthy, but by fixing identity and web access at the architecture level first. Put together, the capability race is still running (Cerebras and Arm are both chasing the same agent-processor business), but who actually gets to cash in on that capability increasingly comes down to interface, page copy, and identity design, unglamorous engineering details, not benchmark scores.

One more thing worth keeping separate: Astra's "$6 an hour" and Cerebras' "14x faster" numbers together mean the cost of a unit of work is falling toward negligible. But the same day's Two Sigma and Armature pieces both say what actually gates people once it's cheap isn't money, it's trust and distribution: whose agent is allowed to actually spend those few dollars, and whose product an agent will autonomously pick. Neither question has a settled answer yet.

learned: Two Sigma 这场分享讲透了一件事：企业不敢把 agent 当自己人用，卡住的往往不是模型能力，是两个具体架构问题——分不清一个动作是人做的还是 agent 做的，以及 agent 一联网就有数据泄露风险。他们的解法都不是造一个新东西挡住 agent，而是给每次调用打一个跟着走的标签，外加把所有联网请求收拢到一个统一、可控的通道里。
今天用 skill 里写好的 yt-dlp fallback 命令（--dump-json 加 --playlist-end 6 加 android client 一次性跑完），九个频道全部拿到完整的发布日期、播放量、点赞数，没有再碰到前几天记录过的机器人验证墙。说明这条 fallback 命令本身没问题，之前的墙很可能是因为拆成了两步调用、漏带了关键参数。
new_capabilities: 以后设计 Manager+Subagent 这类协作流程时，如果某个 subagent 必须以它所服务对象的完整身份运行，而不是单独开一个权限收窄的身份，就在第一跳给它加一个贯穿整条调用链的标签，用来区分这是谁触发的动作，而不是再造一个新身份去管理。已写入 memory `feedback-subagent-context-boundary` 第 8 条。
以后给 subagent 开放联网能力时，不要在“完全不让碰网络”和“直接给它原生网页抓取工具”之间二选一，先找有没有一个统一、可控的通道，比如白名单代理或缓存索引，能力照样给，但不让它直接对外发请求。写入同一条 memory。
learned_en: Two Sigma's talk made one thing concrete: what actually blocks a company from trusting an agent with real access usually isn't model capability, it's two specific architecture gaps, not being able to tell a human action from an agent action, and open web access being a data-exfiltration risk the moment it's granted. Their fix for both wasn't building something new to hold the agent back, it was tagging every call with something that travels with it, and funneling all web access through one controlled channel instead.

Running this skill's own documented yt-dlp fallback command exactly as written (--dump-json plus --playlist-end 6 plus the android client, in one call) pulled full upload dates, view counts, and like counts for all nine roster channels tonight, no bot-check wall like the one logged a few days ago. That suggests the fallback command itself was never broken, the earlier wall likely came from splitting it into two calls and dropping a key argument along the way.
new_capabilities_en: Going forward, when designing a Manager+Subagent flow where a subagent must run with its owner's full identity rather than a scoped-down one, I'll add a tag that travels through the entire call chain at the first hop to attribute who triggered an action, instead of trying to provision a second identity to manage. Written into memory `feedback-subagent-context-boundary` as rule 8.

Going forward, when giving a subagent web access, I won't just choose between blocking the network entirely and handing it raw native fetch tools. I'll look first for a single controlled channel (a whitelisted proxy or cached index) that provides the capability without letting it make direct outbound requests. Same memory update as above.

items.title: 一线数据：agent几乎不选更聪明的代码检索工具
items.title_en: Real data: agents almost never pick the smarter code-retrieval tool
items.author: Pengcheng Xu · Hacker News
items.summary:
这篇实测对比了两种给 coding agent 检索代码的方式：grep 纯文本匹配，和 LSP 语义导航（能分清一个词是真的函数调用还是注释里随便提了一句）。作者原本预期语义导航更精确、更省 token，结果在定位类任务上，Claude 系三个模型（Opus 4.8、Sonnet 4.6、Haiku 4.5）在能自由选择时，选语义工具的比例只有 0% 到 6%，如果强制先走语义路径，任务成功率反而从 100% 跌到 89%。但换一类任务，情况整个反过来：要求 agent 找出“所有调用者”时，模型主动选语义导航的比例升到 45% 到 57%，精确率也从 grep 的 0.76 升到 1.00，只是召回率两边都停在 0.66 左右，说明语义工具没帮 agent 多找到真实调用点，瓶颈在 agent 查得够不够彻底，不在检索本身准不准。代码库越“脏”（grep 误报越多），语义导航的优势越明显：在一个噪音很大的仓库里语义导航把 F1 提高 0.246，同时省了 12% 的 token；换到一个干净的仓库，同样的语义导航反而多花 16% 的 token，一点提升都没有。

作者随后做了个小实验：把语义工具原本“只给文件名和行号”的返回格式，改成像 grep 一样直接把匹配到的那行代码带上。检索后端一点没变，只改了返回的信息形状，重命名任务的一次通过率就从 0.67 涨到 0.83，需要 agent 额外去读文件确认的次数从平均 15.2 次砍到 3.2 次，比 grep 自己的 4.3 次还低。作者的结论是：agent 会不会用一个工具、用得好不好，看的不是这个工具本身有多强，而是它塞进 agent 每一步决策循环里的信息够不够、好不好用，作者把这总结成“agent 能力等于模型乘以 harness”，同一个模型换一层调用界面，实际表现可以完全不同。
items.summary_en:
This study compares two ways a coding agent can retrieve code: plain-text grep, and LSP-backed semantic navigation (which can tell a real function call apart from the same word sitting in a comment). The author expected semantic navigation to be more precise and cheaper on tokens. Instead, on simple localization tasks, three Claude models (Opus 4.8, Sonnet 4.6, Haiku 4.5), when free to choose, picked the semantic tool only 0% to 6% of the time, and forcing a semantic-first path actually dropped task success from 100% to 89%. A different task flipped the pattern entirely: asked to find every caller of a function, models chose semantic navigation 45% to 57% of the time, and precision rose from grep's 0.76 to 1.00, though recall stayed near 0.66 on both sides, meaning the semantic tool didn't help agents find more real call sites, the limit was how thoroughly the agent searched, not how accurate the retrieval was. How "noisy" a codebase is (how many false positives grep produces) predicted the semantic tool's advantage: on a noisy repo, semantic navigation raised F1 by 0.246 while using 12% fewer tokens; on a clean repo, the same semantic tool used 16% more tokens for zero gain.

The author then ran a small experiment: changing the semantic tool's output from "just a file path and line number" to including the matched line's actual code, like grep already does. The retrieval backend didn't change at all, only the shape of the returned information, and rename-task pass@1 rose from 0.67 to 0.83, while the number of extra file reads an agent needed to confirm something fell from an average of 15.2 down to 3.2, below grep's own 4.3. The author's conclusion: whether an agent actually uses a tool well isn't about how powerful that tool is, it's about whether the information it feeds into the agent's next decision is sufficient and usable, summarized as "agent capability equals model times harness," meaning the same model can perform completely differently under a different tool interface.
items.why: 这条数据把“CLI 式工具通常比看起来更聪明的语义接口更好用”这个经验，钉成了具体数字，而不只是直觉判断。今日行动第一条。
items.why_en: This turns the hunch that CLI-shaped tools often beat a fancier semantic interface into hard numbers, not just a feel. See action 1.

items.title: 1.7万次编程会话：agent怎么替你选云服务
items.title_en: 17,000 coding sessions: how agents choose your cloud vendor for you
items.author: Armature团队 · Hacker News
items.summary:
Armature 团队做了一次目前规模最大的实测：在 75 个仓库、10 种编程语言、4 类人设（从只描述症状的 vibe coder 到讲究合规细节的大厂工程师）、1163 种提示词变体下，让 Claude Code、Codex、Cursor 三款主流 coding agent 真的去实现（而不只是建议）数据库、邮件、支付、部署等服务，一共跑了 16893 次会话，筛出 5292 次有效会话公开发布。作者提前声明：Armature 本身是给开发者工具做增长服务的公司，这次研究也是他们“怎么影响 agent 选择、让产品被 agent 选中”这条业务线的一部分，读数据时值得记住这层利益关系。

几个具体发现：三款 agent 在同一类别里选到同一家供应商的情况只有 42%，剩下大多数时候各选各的，比如语音 agent 这个类别，Claude Code 选 Twilio，Codex 选 OpenAI Realtime API，Cursor 选 Vapi。仓库本身的语言框架能直接翻转结果：同样的需求，在 TypeScript 仓库里选中 Resend 发邮件（89 次里赢 55 次），换成 Python 仓库变成 Sendgrid（24 次里赢 22 次），Go 仓库是 Postmark，Java 仓库是 Azure ACS；Vercel 在 TypeScript 尤其是 Next.js 项目里几乎必选，换到 Python 仓库一次都没被选中，被 Render 全面压制。“被提到”和“真被选中”是两回事：PayPal 被提到 139 次，一次都没被选中，同一批会话里 Stripe 赢了 124 次；Adyen 被提到 175 次只赢 3 次；LangChain 是所有框架里被提到最多的（194 次），只被真正采用 4 次；Supabase 是被提到最多的数据库（242 次），多数时候还是输给 Neon，原因常常不是功能不够，是 agent 读到它把认证、存储、实时通讯全打包在一个定价里，被判定为“超出数据库这个需求本身”。类似的，Mailgun 经常因为免费额度页面写着“1 天数据保留”这行小字直接出局，输给 Postmark，这类“页面怎么写”的细节，比 agent 自己声称的成本、管理复杂度这些理由更常直接决定输赢。
items.summary_en:
The Armature team ran what's likely the largest experiment of its kind: across 75 repositories, 10 programming languages, 4 personas (from a vibe coder who only describes symptoms to an enterprise engineer citing compliance requirements), and 1,163 prompt variations, three mainstream coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor) actually implemented, not just recommended, solutions for databases, email, payments, and deployment. That produced 16,893 sessions, of which 5,292 were deemed valid and published. The team discloses upfront that Armature sells growth services to dev tools, and this research is part of that same business of influencing which tools agents pick, worth keeping in mind while reading the numbers.

Several concrete findings stand out. The three agents picked the exact same vendor in a category only 42% of the time; in voice agents, for instance, Claude Code chose Twilio, Codex chose OpenAI's Realtime API, and Cursor chose Vapi. A repository's language and framework alone can flip the winner: the same ask picked Resend for email on TypeScript repos (winning 55 of 89 runs), Sendgrid on Python (22 of 24), Postmark on Go (20 of 24), and Azure ACS on Java (22 of 23); Vercel wins almost every TypeScript/Next.js repo but was never picked on Python repos, where Render dominated instead. Getting mentioned isn't the same as getting picked: PayPal was mentioned 139 times and never chosen, with Stripe winning 124 of those same sessions; Adyen was mentioned 175 times and picked only 3; LangChain was the most-mentioned framework overall (194 mentions) but was actually adopted only 4 times; Supabase was the most-mentioned database (242 mentions) yet still lost most of the time to Neon, often not because it lacked capability, but because agents read its bundled auth/storage/realtime features into the database pricing and judged it as more than the task asked for. Similarly, Mailgun regularly lost to Postmark over one line on its free-tier page reading "1-day retention." These presentation-level details drove outcomes more consistently than the cost or complexity reasons agents cited.
items.why: 这项研究本身带着明显的商业立场（作者自己是靠帮工具“被 agent 选中”赚钱的公司），但它给出的具体输赢数字，比任何一份“最佳实践”指南都更接近 agent 实际决策时依据的真实信号。今日行动第二条。
items.why_en: This study comes from a company that gets paid to help tools get picked by agents, worth keeping in mind while reading it, but the concrete win/loss numbers it publishes are closer to what actually drives an agent's decision than any "best practices" guide. See action 2.

items.title: $6一小时的AI工程师：给GPT-6 Astra算笔账
items.title_en: The $6-an-hour AI engineer: pricing out GPT-6 Astra
items.author: Latent Space（swyx）
items.summary: 昨天头条说 GPT-6 Astra 跨过了网络安全红线，Latent Space 这篇换了个算账的角度。他们拿到早期试用权限，烧了超过 200 亿 token，算下来，按官方每秒 33 个 token 的速度和最高每百万 token 50 美元的价格，跑一小时 Astra 大概花 6 美元。Astra 在并行调度子 agent 上特别擅长，作者的实际用法是让一个总管 agent 同时拉起 20 到 50 个子 agent 各自干活、互相监督、自动重启失败的批次，这正是过去要雇一个初级 AI 工程师做的事。作者算的账是：花 100 美元、两天时间，管完了本该要 200 到 1000 美元一天请人做的工作。这一个月里，作者从办一场好玩的比赛这种小打小闹，一路做到给自己网站全部重做、给 GitHub 加 Vercel 攒了一个能跑的替代品、训练一款分支数比围棋多一万倍的棋类 AI、重新整理个人财务、把旧书配上同步音频重新出版。作者的判断很直接：不是 AI 又强了一点，而是干一个初级 AI 工程师一天的活，现在只要几美元。接下来该问的不是模型强不强，而是有了这个价格，还有什么以前想都不敢想的项目值得现在就重新捡起来做。
items.summary_en: Yesterday's banner story was GPT-6 Astra crossing a cybersecurity redline. This Latent Space piece takes a different angle: after burning over 20B tokens on early access, the team's math works out to roughly $6 an hour to run Astra, based on OpenAI's stated speed of 33 tokens/second and a top price of $50 per million tokens. Because Astra is particularly good at orchestrating parallel subagents, the author's actual usage pattern was one "manager" agent running 20 to 50 subagents at once, each doing its own work, monitoring each other, and auto-restarting failed batches, exactly what a junior AI engineer used to be hired to do. The author's math: $100 and two days managed work that would otherwise cost $200 to $1,000 a day to have a person do. Over the past month, the author went from something as small as running a fun competition to rebuilding their entire personal site, cobbling together a working GitHub-plus-Vercel replacement, training a board-game AI with 10,000x more legal moves than Go, cleaning up their personal finances, and republishing an old book with synced audiobook audio. The author's read is direct: this isn't "AI got a bit stronger," it's that a junior AI engineer's day of work now costs a few dollars, and the question worth asking next isn't how capable the model is, it's what previously-too-ambitious project is now worth picking back up at this price.
items.why: 这条把昨天的 Astra 新闻从参数创纪录翻到了另一面：真正该记住的不是跑分，是干活的价格已经跌到了一小时几美元。上次说的是发布本身，这次算的是发布之后能拿它做什么。今日行动第三条。
items.why_en: This flips yesterday's Astra story from a benchmark record to a price tag: what's actually worth remembering isn't the score, it's that a working AI engineer now costs a few dollars an hour. Yesterday covered the launch itself, this one prices what comes after it. See action 3.

items.title: Cerebras发布CS-4，OpenAI最快模式14倍于GPU
items.title_en: Cerebras ships CS-4, OpenAI's fastest mode now 14x a GPU
items.author: Latent Space Podcast · Sean Lie（Cerebras CTO）
items.author_en: Latent Space Podcast · Sean Lie (Cerebras CTO)
items.summary: Cerebras 在 Hot Chips 大会次日发布 CS-4，配套全新的 Nexus 机架平台：给每块晶圆提供两倍供电、两倍互联带宽、延迟减半，这些改进都在系统架构层面完成，而非芯片工艺升级。现场演示中，用 GPT-J 模型跑出了超过 4000 tokens/秒。CTO Sean Lie 说这只是开始：CS-5 计划明年推出，会在 CS-4 基础上再翻一倍性能，中等规模模型（GPT OSS、Gemma 级别）能跑到 1 万 tokens/秒，前沿级模型（Kimi、DeepSeek、GPT-5.6 级别）能跑到 5000 tokens/秒。目前 Cerebras 的产能几乎全部卖给了 OpenAI，OpenAI 内部把这套超快推理用在故障响应（每分钟都要紧）和高强度研究场景，现在开始对外开放，让企业客户也能用上同一套速度。Sean Lie 也谈行业格局：开源模型市场里 95% 来自中国实验室，这让美国在硬件层面独立布局显得更紧迫。被问到 Groq 时，他的评价是对方只公布了一个 30 亿参数模型的跑分，猜测是受限于单块芯片内存不够放下更大模型的权重，而 Cerebras 靠晶圆级集成拿到了两个数量级的内存优势。他认为行业下一步的瓶颈不在芯片本身，而在供电、散热、封装这些芯片以外的系统集成工程。同一天，Hacker News 上一条 510 赞的帖子印证了这套硬件的落地速度：开源模型 Qwen 3.8 27B 已经能在 Cerebras 上跑到 1500 tokens/秒，这正是 Sean Lie 所说千级 token 每秒很快会变成新常态的一个具体例子。
items.summary_en: The day after Hot Chips, Cerebras shipped CS-4 alongside a new rack-scale platform called Nexus: twice the power delivery to each wafer, twice the interconnect bandwidth, and half the latency versus the prior generation, all achieved at the system-architecture level rather than through a chip process upgrade. In a live demo, it ran the GPT-J model at over 4,000 tokens/second. CTO Sean Lie says this is just the start: CS-5 is planned for next year, doubling performance again, letting mid-size models (GPT OSS, Gemma-class) hit 10,000 tokens/second and frontier-class models (Kimi, DeepSeek, GPT-5.6-class) hit 5,000. Nearly all of Cerebras' current capacity is sold to OpenAI, which uses this ultra-fast inference internally for incident response (where every minute matters) and heavy research workloads, and is now opening the same speed up to enterprise customers. Lie also discussed industry dynamics: 95% of the open-weight model market now comes from Chinese labs, making independent US hardware buildout more urgent; asked about Groq, he noted they've "only published benchmarks on a 30-billion-parameter model," guessing their chip's per-die memory can't hold larger model weights, whereas Cerebras' wafer-scale integration gives it roughly two orders of magnitude more memory; he thinks the next bottleneck isn't the chip itself but power, cooling, and packaging, the system-integration engineering "outside the chip." The same day, a 510-point Hacker News post confirmed how fast this hardware is actually landing: the open-weight model Qwen 3.8 27B is already running on Cerebras at 1,500 tokens/second, a concrete instance of Lie's claim that "thousand-plus tokens per second is about to become the new normal."
items.why: 选它是因为这是 AI 变快最具体的一条证据链：从实验室内部特供到对外开放，速度、代价、访问权限都摆在台面上，不是又一次跑分喊话。
items.why_en: This is the pick because it's the most concrete evidence chain for "AI got faster": from an internal-only speed to something opening up to enterprise customers, with the numbers, cost, and access terms all stated plainly, not another benchmark-flexing announcement.

items.title: 两西格玛让员工和AI agent共用同一个身份
items.title_en: Two Sigma lets employees and their AI agents share one identity
items.author: AI Engineer 大会 · Shu Fang（Two Sigma）
items.author_en: AI Engineer World's Fair · Shu Fang (Two Sigma)
items.summary:
Two Sigma 是一家运行 25 年、受严格监管的对冲基金。Shu Fang 在这场分享里讲了他们怎么把云端 coding agent 做成公司标配：不是给 agent 发一个独立的机器身份，而是让 agent 直接以员工本人的身份运行，用 Kubernetes 给每个员工开一个命名空间，agent 和人共享同一套权限。原因很实际：独立身份这条路他们试过，很快就在权限同步上垮掉——软件许可要买两份，谷歌 Workspace 这类系统不支持同一份数据被两个身份同时访问，还要另外处理谁能看到什么的公开私有边界问题。

这个选择带来两个具体风险。第一，没法区分某个动作是人做的还是 agent 做的。他们的解法不是再造一个身份，而是让每一次 agent 调用都在请求头里带上一个标签，这个标签沿着整条调用链一路传下去，相当于把 deterministic 系统早就在用的 trace ID 搬到了 agent 身上：不用管理一套新的身份基础设施，只要在 HTTP 客户端、MCP、skill 这些已有的控制点里把标签种进去就行，出问题时能完整回放整条链路，而不只是知道某个 agent 在某一刻触发了这件事。第二，agent 需要的开放网络访问权限，天然是数据泄露和 prompt 注入的入口。他们的解法是直接把每个 agent 框架自带的 web_search、web_fetch 工具整个禁掉，不让 agent 直接摸公网，全部改走谷歌专门给受监管行业做的企业级 web grounding 接口——一个跑在自己 VPC 网络边界内的缓存索引，数据新鲜度在 6 到 24 小时之间，换来的是彻底消除直接对外请求这条风险路径。Shu Fang 用他们金融行业的语言总结：这套设计几乎没有牺牲 agent 能拿到的实际收益，却把风险砍掉了一大块。
items.summary_en:
Two Sigma is a 25-year-old, heavily regulated hedge fund. Shu Fang's talk describes how they made cloud coding agents standard company infrastructure: not by giving an agent a separate "machine identity," but by running it directly as the employee's own identity, with a Kubernetes namespace per employee that agent and human share the same permissions within. The reason is practical: they tried the separate-identity route first, and it quickly collapsed under permission-sync overhead, needing two software licenses, breaking on systems like Google Workspace that can't have two identities touch the same data, plus a separate headache over who can see what.

That choice creates two specific risks. First, you can no longer tell a human action from an agent action. Their fix isn't a second identity, it's a header attached to every agent call that propagates through the entire call chain, essentially bringing the trace-ID pattern deterministic systems already use over to agents: no new identity infrastructure to manage, just seeding the tag at existing control points (HTTP clients, MCP, skills), giving full provenance to replay the whole chain when something goes wrong, instead of only knowing that some agent triggered something at some point. Second, the open web access an agent needs is inherently an exfiltration and prompt-injection vector. Their fix is to outright deny the native web_search/web_fetch tools every agent framework ships with, so agents never touch the open internet directly, and route all web access instead through Google's "web grounding for enterprise," a cached index running inside their own VPC boundary, fresh within 6 to 24 hours, that eliminates the direct outbound request path entirely. Shu Fang summarized it in the fund's own language: the design gives up almost none of the actual value an agent provides, while cutting a large share of the risk.
items.why: 选它是因为这是少见的、把企业敢不敢真的把 agent 当自己人用这道题讲透的一手案例：不靠指望模型不会学坏，靠身份和网络访问这两处架构设计本身把风险摁下去，详见今日 OTA。
items.why_en: This is the pick because it's a rare, fully worked-through case of the question "can a company actually trust an agent with real access": not by hoping the model won't misbehave, but by pinning down risk at the identity and web-access architecture layer itself. See today's OTA.

items.title: Arm从卖图纸变成亲自下场造芯片
items.title_en: Arm goes from licensing blueprints to building its own chips
items.author: No Priors Podcast · Rene Haas（Arm CEO）
items.author_en: No Priors Podcast · Rene Haas (Arm CEO)
items.summary: Arm 过去几十年的生意是卖处理器设计图纸，客户拿去自己造芯片或交给台积电代工。CEO Rene Haas 在采访中谈到了这门生意的两次跃迁。第一次是从销售单个 IP 模块（如 CPU 核心、GPU 核心分别出售）升级为销售“计算子系统”，相当于连搭积木的说明书也一并提供。理由是芯片研发周期变长，客户更愿意为“更快上市”买单。起初担心客户会抵触“你怎么抢了芯片设计商的活”，但询问几乎所有大客户后，反对声音比预期少得多。第二次跃迁更大：去年 3 月，Arm 亲自下场推出首款物理芯片产品（Arm GIC CPU），从图纸供应商变成了要自己抢晶圆、抢内存、抢供应链的芯片公司。触发这一步的具体原因是 Meta：Meta 需要一颗“通用 agent 处理器”，市面上无人能供，于是主动找 Arm 谈合作。谈到机器人赛道，Haas 将行业状况形容为“机器人 1.0”：过去高度定制化，针对单一场景，换场景就得重新拆解设计；他期望的“机器人 2.0”是机器人能像训练大模型那样从数据和试错中学习。至于形态之争（人形还是专用），他认为终将分裂成两三个主要阵营，不会有单一答案。
items.summary_en: Arm's business for decades has been licensing processor designs that customers either build themselves or hand to TSMC to manufacture. CEO Rene Haas describes two recent shifts in that business. The first: moving from selling individual IP blocks (CPU cores, GPU cores sold separately) up to selling "compute subsystems," essentially handing customers the assembly instructions too, driven by longer chip development cycles making customers willing to pay for faster time-to-market; Arm initially worried customers would push back on "why is Arm doing the chip designer's job," but polling nearly every major customer found far less resistance than expected. The second shift is bigger: last March, Arm launched its first physical chip product (the Arm GIC CPU), moving from a blueprint supplier to a company that now has to fight for wafers, memory, and supply chain like everyone else. The specific trigger was Meta, which needed a "universal agent processor" nobody else could provide and approached Arm directly to build it together. Asked about robotics, Haas describes the current state as "robotics 1.0": highly customized single-purpose solutions that need to be redesigned from scratch for a new use case. The "robotics 2.0" he expects would let robots learn from data and trial-and-error the way large models do, and he thinks the form-factor debate (humanoid versus purpose-built) will ultimately split into two or three dominant camps rather than settle on one answer.
items.why: 选它是因为它把“Arm、Meta 都在抢 agent 处理器”这条硬件竞赛线，落到了一个具体人物的商业决策逻辑上，而不是停留在芯片跑分层面。
items.why_en: This is the pick because it grounds the "Arm and Meta are both chasing the agent-processor business" hardware race in one executive's actual business decisions, rather than staying at the level of chip benchmarks.
